title: Vocational education systems are being pushed to adapt faster to the green transition while qualification, teaching, and adult-training capacity remain uneven
source_unit: OECD, Vocational education and training (VET) in transition: VET policy under energy constraints, September 2026
geography: OECD countries and partner economies; vocational education, green-transition skills, teachers, workers, and adult retraining systems

observations.period: September 2026; VET under green-transition skill pressure

denominator.unit: OECD policy-paper synthesis of VET systems under energy and green-transition change

transition_pressure.value: technological and industrial shifts create new occupations, transform existing ones, and render some jobs obsolete

qualification_lag.value: qualification-update processes struggle to keep pace with innovation

competence_gaps.value: VET programmes face gaps in technical, foundational, and sustainability competences

observations.method: OECD policy analysis drawing on evidence from OECD countries; it is a synthesis and policy framework rather than a single causal evaluation.
observations.uncertainty: The paper identifies cross-country challenges but does not imply identical transition speeds, qualification lags, or labour-market effects across sectors and places.
observations.subgroup: VET learners, workers in transition-exposed occupations, employers, training providers, qualification authorities, and workers with different foundational skills.
observations.counterinterpretation: Slow qualification processes can protect quality, safety, and occupational legitimacy; speed without employer, worker, and public oversight could reduce trust in credentials.

observations.period: September 2026; teacher capability and adult-training participation

teacher_gap.value: VET teachers may lack familiarity with emerging technologies

adult_participation.value: training participation remains persistently low among workers most exposed to structural change

support_tools.value: targeted training for VET teachers and trainers, modular adult learning, and personalised career guidance are identified as policy tools

observations.method: OECD comparative policy synthesis of VET teachers, trainers, adult learners, transition exposure, and proposed policy tools.
observations.uncertainty: The paper does not establish why exposed workers participate less, whether modular learning removes cost and time barriers, or which teacher-training models produce durable results.
observations.subgroup: VET teachers and trainers, older workers, workers in carbon-intensive or transition-exposed sectors, adults with low foundational skills, and people needing career guidance.
observations.counterinterpretation: Workers may avoid training because of employer scheduling, income loss, care, geography, distrust, or weak expected returns—not simply because provision lacks modularity.

observations.period: September 2026; modularity, guidance, and adaptation capacity

skills_anticipation.value: skills anticipation is identified as a tool for aligning VET with changing demand

modular_learning.value: modular learning pathways can support adult retraining and make qualification updates more flexible

career_guidance.value: personalised career guidance is proposed to help learners and workers navigate transition

social_partnership.value: responsive VET requires engagement among employers, learners, providers, and social partners

observations.method: Policy-paper synthesis of skills intelligence, qualification updates, modular learning, teacher development, and guidance approaches.
observations.uncertainty: These are proposed or identified policy tools, not evidence that modularity or anticipation automatically produces equitable retraining or employment.
observations.subgroup: Young learners, adult retrainers, employers, social partners, regional skills bodies, VET institutions, and workers navigating occupation change.
observations.counterinterpretation: Modularity can increase flexibility but also fragment credentials, shift navigation costs to learners, or weaken broad foundational learning if not connected to progression and recognized qualifications.

related_sources.claim: OECD DOI and publication citation for VET in transition.

boundary: This record adds a VET-transition route from industrial and energy-system change through qualification agility, teacher capacity, adult participation, modular retraining, guidance, and labour-market adaptation. It does not establish causal training effects, equal access, realized green employment, or that speed should replace quality and social-partner governance.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official OECD publication page reviewed for transition pressure, qualification-update lag, competence gaps, teacher capability, low training participation, policy tools, modular learning, career guidance, and social-partnership routes.
